newsitem.title: UK: Aerospace seen lifting Smiths profits.
newsitem.headline: Aerospace seen lifting Smiths profits.

text.p: Avionics to medical and industrial products group Smiths Industries Plc said on Wednesday that stronger demand from aircraft manufacturers helped boost its half-year profits by 15 percent and it expects earnings to continue growing.

Group profits for the six months to February 1 rose to 80.2 million pounds ($130.4 million) from 69.5 million pounds last year on sales up six percent at 495.3 million pounds. An exceptional gain on a property sale added a further 4.0 million pounds to the pretax result.
The dividend was raised 10 percent to 6.15 pence a share in line with market forecasts, on post-exceptional earnings up 22 percent at 18.9 pence a share.
The shares were up 5-1/2 pence at 801p by 0920 GMT but were off early highs of 808p.
"The results were solid," said Andy Chambers, industry analyst at SocGen. "A fairly confident statement and good progress in the aerospace division, which is encouraging."
Chambers noted the relatively flat performance of the Medical Systems division but said the Industrial group had performed well.

The company said it was now starting to enjoy the first fruits of recovery in output by aircraft manufacturers and the rationalisation of its Aerospace division during the lean years of recession now promised a further boost in profit margins as sales rise.

Operating profits at the division rose 5.7 million pounds to 22.9 million in the half year on sales up 12.7 million at 184.1 million pounds, an increase in operating margin of 2.4 points to 12.4 percent.

"If at the early stage of the (upturn in the aerospace business) cycle we can be improving margins like this then I would expect to see that improvement sustained," chairman Sir Roger Hurn told Reuters in an interview.
"At the peak of the last boom (in the aerospace industry cycle) in 1992 we were making between 15 and 16 percent margins. The fact is that this is the start of an upturn," he said.

Operating margins at Smiths' famously profitable Medical Systems division rose to 22.4 percent from 21.6 percent a year ago. The company said exports by the division, which specialises in single-use products and surgical equipment, were held back by the strength of sterling and sales dipped 3.7 million pounds to 142.2 million pounds.
But operating profits rose 300,000 pounds to 31.9 million pounds.
Hurn said profits at the division would probably have been about two million pounds higher had it not been for the effects of sterling on exports.

"It is a premium margin business," Hurn said. "Our policy particularly over this period has been not to chase sales at the expense of margin but to make sure that we make quality sales and maintain margin," he said.

Operating profits at the Industrial division, where products range from flexible tubing to domestic electrical timer switches, rose five million pounds to 26.6 million on sales up 20.1 million at 169 million pounds.
Hurn said the impact of sterling's strength on the group's overall results was limited because more than half of the company's manufacturing was based overseas.
He estimated that the overall impact was to reduce profits by about two million pounds in translation of foreign earnings and by a further two million due to the medical division's export business.
"I don't think it's a very big effect. We're less effected by this than some other UK-based companies," he said.
He said the company would also go on seeking growth from making further bolt-on acquisitions but declined to say when and where the next deal might get done.

"Yes, we have got the same appetite to go on making them, out of strong internal cash generation, and we have an awful lot to look at. But we are very selective," he said. Net debt at the end of January stood at 27.8 million pounds, up from 13.5 million a year ago, against shareholders funds of 243 million pounds and after 18.7 million of cash was spent on further acquisitions in the half year.
